item.title: Macroscopic study of $\phi$-mesic nuclei in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 7 TeV with the PACIAE model
item.description: arXiv:2610.12935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A macroscopic method of the parton and hadron cascade model PACIAE combined with the coalescence model DCPC is employed to study the $\phi$-mesic nuclei in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 7 TeV for the first time in this work. Based on the final hadronic states of $pp$ collisions simulated by the PACIAE model, the $\phi$-mesic nuclei: $\mathrm{^3_{\phi} H}(\phi-pn)$, $\mathrm{^4_{\phi} H}(\phi-pnn)$, and $\mathrm{^4_{\phi} He}(\phi-ppn)$ are recombined by the DCPC model with constituents of protons, neutrons, and $\phi$ mesons. Their yields, transverse momentum spectra, and rapidity distributions are simulated separately. These theoretical predictions call for experimental confirmation.
item.dc:creator: Qiang Wang, Zhi-Lei She, An-Ke Lei, Dai-Mei Zhou, Wen-Chao Zhang, Hua Zheng, Li-Lin Zhu, Yu-Liang Yan, Zhong-Qi Wang, Ben-Hao Sa

item.title: Octupole correlations in the excited $0^+$ states and two-neutron transfers in actinide nuclei
item.description: arXiv:2610.13048v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Impacts of octupole correlations on low-energy excited $0^+$ states and two-neutron transfer intensities in Ra and Th isotopes are analyzed within the interacting boson model, using the Hamiltonian parameters that are obtained from microscopic nuclear density functional theory calculations. Incorporating the octupole degree of freedom in the model is shown to give an overall reasonable description of the ground-state-band energy levels and to lower the $0^+_2$ ones significantly. The calculation yields a number of excited $0^+$ states, most of which are formed by the configurations of more than one octupole boson. Octupole correlations make significant contributions to the $0^+_1 \to 0^+_2$ $(p,t)$ and $(t,p)$ transfer intensities in those nuclei in which the octupole collectivity is most enhanced. Behaviors of the predicted transfer intensities with the increasing neutron number along the isotopic chain reflect nuclear structural evolution.
item.dc:creator: Kosuke Nomura

item.title: Levy-shaped femtoscopic sources from an exact solution of relativistic hydrodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.13352v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An important goal of high-energy physics is to better understand the spacetime structure of particle emitting sources created in heavy-ion collisions. For a fraction of a second a special form of matter, the so-called quark-gluon plasma (QGP) is created, which can be examined with the toolkit of femtoscopy. With the measurement of correlation functions it was determined that L\'evy distributions describe the shape of QGP sources the most accurately, however, based on hydrodynamics Gaussian distributions are typically expected. In this article we showcase an exact solution of the equations of relativistic hydrodynamics, which aims to resolve this puzzle by providing L\'evy distributions directly from hydrodynamics. A detailed analysis reveals whether the predictions of this solution are in accordance with observations.
item.dc:creator: Bence Szentkuti, Mate Csanad

item.title: Constrained coupled-cluster computations yield negative-parity rotational bands
item.description: arXiv:2610.13449v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many deformed nuclei exhibit low-lying rotational bands with negative parity. In mean-field calculations, such bands follow from symmetry restoration when the variational solution spontaneously breaks parity. However, they can also be computed in cases where the breaking of parity is not spontaneous but rather enforced by an octupole constraint. In this paper, we extend these techniques to coupled-cluster computations. We introduce octupole-constrained coupled-cluster theory, which explicitly breaks the parity of the correlated intrinsic state and restores parity and angular momentum as good quantum numbers by projection after variation. We perform coupled-cluster singles-and-doubles (CCSD) computations for $^{20}$Ne using two- and three-nucleon forces from chiral effective field theory. The energies of the positive-parity ground-state rotational band are close to data and depend only weakly on the constrained octupole moment and the Hartree--Fock reference. In contrast, the energies of the negative-parity rotational band are more sensitive to these auxiliary quantities.
item.dc:creator: Gaute Hagen, Benjamin Bally, Thomas Papenbrock

item.title: Final-state centrality in relativistic heavy-ion simulations from neural networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.13828v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Experiments in relativistic heavy-ion collisions determine centrality from final-state quantities, usually the charged-particle multiplicity. Performing the same in hydrodynamic simulations requires millions of events, which is impractical for state-of-the-art hybrid models, and centrality is therefore commonly approximated by the initial entropy or energy. We show that neural networks trained on a few hundred hybrid events predict the event-by-event multiplicity and mean transverse momentum $[p_T]$ with relative errors of 1--2\%, which makes it possible to generate millions of collisions at a small fraction of the cost of the full simulation. For Pb--Pb collisions at $2.76$~TeV and Au--Au collisions at $200$~GeV, the initial-state and final-state definitions select nearly the same events in 10\%-wide classes, but up to 20\% of the events change class when the classes are 1\% wide. We then compute the fluctuations of $[p_T]$ and its Pearson correlations with a proxy of the elliptic flow, estimated from the initial eccentricity, and with multiplicity. The first correlation is insensitive to how centrality is defined, while the second changes substantially. The approach can be applied at every design point of Bayesian analyses at modest additional cost.
item.dc:creator: Anibal Bezerra, Fernando G. Gardim

item.title: Impact of ab initio E1 strength on neutron capture rates along the nickel isotopic chain
item.description: arXiv:2610.13868v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nucleosynthesis simulations of the r-process require neutron capture rates for neutron-rich nuclei, many of which lie beyond experimental reach. Predicting these rates relies on theoretical calculations of the low-energy electric dipole (E1) strength near the neutron threshold. We present the first ab initio computation of the E1 strength along the nickel isotopic chain, for $^{58}$Ni and the even-even isotopes $^{68-80}$Ni. The E1 strength is obtained with the Lorentz integral transform coupled-cluster (LIT-CC) method, extended to axially symmetric reference states to reach open-shell nuclei, using two- and three-nucleon interactions from chiral effective field theory. The approach is benchmarked against the measured photoabsorption cross section of $^{58}$Ni and the E1 strength of $^{68}$Ni. Along the chain we find low-lying E1 strength above the neutron threshold that grows with neutron number. Including it in the reaction code TALYS enhances the neutron capture rates forming $^{68-78}$Ni between 3 and 10 GK, with an effect that increases with temperature and neutron number and an uncertainty dominated by the inversion of the integral transform. For $^{80}$Ni, where strong pygmy dipole strength lies just above threshold, the enhancement sets in already around 0.5 GK. Together, these results open the way to ab initio input for neutron capture rates along isotopic chains far from stability.
item.dc:creator: Francesca Bonaiti, Joanna E. Sobczyk

item.title: Mass and decay angles in the $\Xi_c$--$\Xi_c'$ mixing tension: Virtual hybrids and a single-direction criterion
item.description: arXiv:2610.12525v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the relation between mixing angles obtained from mass calculations and those inferred from decay analyses of the $\Xi_c$--$\Xi_c'$ system. Within a constituent-quark model, we compare three definitions: a spin-component probability angle, a common-source overlap angle, and an SU(3)-breaking mass-operator angle. The probability angle is $3.11^\circ$, while the latter two definitions give $2.48$--$2.58^\circ$; a second parameter set gives $2.38$--$2.49^\circ$. The change of definition reduces, but does not remove, the difference from the lattice values $1.2(1)^\circ$ and $0.810(50)(200)^\circ$. We then include virtual $qsQg$ states coupled to the conventional $qsQ$ states, where $q=u,d$ and $Q=c,b$. In the tested orbital-$S$-wave model, a chromomagnetic transition containing both $j_{Qg}=1/2$ and $3/2$ raises the source and mass-operator charm angles to $2.67$--$3.16^\circ$ when its strength is normalized to reference short-range mass shifts. The hybrid probability remains below $1.7\%$, and the corresponding bottom angles are $0.42$--$0.48^\circ$. We also give a single-direction condition for the induced mass correction to be proportional to a single rank-one projector. This condition concerns the mass operator, not a universal angle for decay amplitudes. Eliminating the hybrid sector changes the current operator as well as the Hamiltonian; we derive this relation but do not calculate process-dependent decay angles. The results include projected hyperfine coefficients and energy-cut sums for comparisons in specified continuum and lattice matching schemes.
item.dc:creator: Sanghoon Kim, Gihwan Nam, Jongheon Baek

item.title: Dijet hadrochemistry: tomography of jet-induced medium excitation and diffusion wake
item.description: arXiv:2610.13046v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Energetic partons traversing the quark-gluon plasma in relativistic heavy-ion collisions induce a medium response that modifies the production of associated hadrons, whose chemical composition provides a sensitive probe of this response. We study jet-associated hadrochemistry using the coupled linear Boltzmann transport and hydrodynamics model with a hybrid hadronization scheme that combines Cooper--Frye particlization, quark coalescence and string fragmentation. For inclusive charged jets in $p+p$ and 0--10\% central Pb+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=5.02$~TeV, the calculated in-cone $K/\pi$ and $p/\pi$ ratios are enhanced in Pb+Pb relative to $p+p$ collisions, consistent with preliminary ALICE measurements, with coalescence between shower and thermal partons providing a substantial contribution. Extending the analysis to dijet events, we predict that both ratios are enhanced around the leading and subleading jets, more strongly around the subleading jet and more pronounced for larger radial size. After mixed-event acceptance correction and sideband background subtraction, the yields of associated pions, kaons and protons all become negative near $|\Delta\phi|\simeq\pi/2$, signaling a depletion caused by the diffusion wake. The $K/\pi$ and $p/\pi$ ratios of these deficits remain finite and exceed the $p+p$ values around the jet peaks, indicating that the missing hadrons originate from jet-excited medium. These results establish dijet hadrochemistry as an experimentally accessible tomographic probe of jet-induced medium excitation and the diffusion wake.
item.dc:creator: Cong Yi, Xiang-Yu Wu, Zhong Yang, Pi Duan, Guang-You Qin, Xin-Nian Wang, Wenbin Zhao

item.title: nCTEQ26 nuclear parton distribution functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.13633v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present the new release of nuclear parton distribution functions (nPDFs) from the nCTEQ collaboration: nCTEQ26. In this global analysis, we combine our recent, more selective studies of different experimental measurements and extend them to determine a modern set of nPDFs based on the largest selection of data considered to date. This selection includes neutral- and charged-current deep-inelastic scattering (DIS), fixed-target Drell-Yan, and a large variety of collider data from RHIC and LHC Runs I and II. On the theoretical side, we match this considerably extended kinematic range with a new nPDF parametrization that combines a flexible functional form of the x-dependence with a quadratic logarithmic nuclear A-dependence as well as target-mass and deuteron corrections for the reliable inclusion of high-x DIS data. Following our previous successful work, we partially employ a data-driven approach that allows us to not only include open heavy-quark data, but also quarkonium data. In addition, we establish the consistency of this approach by comparing it to an alternative fit based on perturbative predictions of open heavy-quark data alone. We determine the uncertainties of our nCTEQ26 nPDFs with a Hessian error analysis, test their reliability by comparing our nPDFs to other, similar recent analyses, and make predictions for current and future experimental measurements that have not been included in the analysis.
item.dc:creator: nCTEQ Collaboration, K. Greve, T. Je\v{z}o, A. Kusina, J. Wissmann, M. Klasen, K. Kova\v{r}\'ik, C. L\'eger, J. G. Morf\'in, F. I. Olness, P. Risse, I. Schienbein, J. Y. Yu

item.title: Anomaly induced transport in holographic superconductors
item.description: arXiv:2610.13727v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the anomaly-induced transport properties of a holographic superconductor exhibiting spontaneous symmetry breaking. The holographic model incorporates vector and axial gauge fields, an additional non-anomalous $U(1)$ symmetry, and a charged scalar field that drives the phase transition. Working in the probe limit, we numerically construct the superconducting background under two alternative scalar field quantizations, corresponding to operators with scaling dimensions $\Delta=1$ and $\Delta=3$ (denoted as the $O_1$ and $O_2$ theories, respectively). Using Kubo formulae, we compute the chiral magnetic conductivities and examine their response to the scalar condensate. Our findings demonstrate that spontaneous symmetry breaking allows anomaly-induced transport to extend beyond anomalous currents, significantly impacting the non-anomalous sector as well. Remarkably, this effect appears in both theories, indicating that the influence on the non-anomalous sector is independent of the chosen quantization. The comparison of our numerical results with the analytical limits for $O_i \to 0$ and $O_i \to \infty$ $(i=1,2)$ reveals consistent behavior across both theories.
item.dc:creator: Ashis Tamang, Nishal Rai, Javier Esteban, Eugenio Megias

item.title: Adiabatic evolution of hadronic neutron stars
item.description: arXiv:2610.13926v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we compute several structural properties of static and rotating neutron stars, considering both rigid and differential rotation. To this end, we use a finite-temperature beta-stable equation of state (EOS) extending the zero-temperature hadronic EOS derived by Fortin et al. (2017). We account for the formation of hyperons and the presence of a neutrino-trapped component. Our goal is to provide insights into the long-term evolution of a protoneutron star (PNS) formed after a core-collapse supernova (CCSN) or a remnant resulting from a binary neutron star merger (BNSM). The EOS is derived using a relativistic mean-field quantum many-body theory within the Hartree approximation. Coupling constants are determined using experimental data on hypernuclei and hypernuclear matter to better account for uncertainties in hyperon single-particle potentials. Our EOS models reproduce the typical features of cold neutron stars and PNSs for nucleonic and hyperonic compositions. In particular, they are consistent with measured masses (2.01 M_sun and 2.14 M_sun for PSR J0348+0432 and PSR J0740+6620) and dimensionless tidal deformabilities from GW170817. Thermal contributions act differently depending on composition and rotation state. Finally, our evolutionary scheme provides a simple way to interpret the long-term evolution of BNSM remnants or PNSs from CCSNe, complementing dynamical simulations unable to cover full evolutionary timescales.
item.dc:creator: Domenico Logoteta, Francesco Zeno Constanzo, Ignazio Bombaci, Sebastiano Bernuzzi, Albino Perego, David Radice

item.title: Geometric factors in the volume dependence of many-body bound states
item.description: arXiv:2511.06726v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: I derive the volume dependence of bound states from a cluster-cluster picture with nucleon degrees of freedom. A constant factor called the geometric factor appears in the generalization from point-like particles to clusters. I show that this factor is obtained explicitly when the underlying overlap integral is evaluated directly in the original many-body space. I achieve this by constructing Jacobi coordinates on the lattice with periodic boundary conditions. The derivation requires only the interaction between the clusters to be short-ranged, with the nonperturbative Coulomb force included. The factor emerges as a geometric property of the many-body configuration space rather than a multiplicity of physical channels. I validate my derivation using many-body calculations; in particular, I find this factor to be essential in extracting asymptotic normalization constants from lattice calculations of the \isotope[16]{O} ground state.
item.dc:creator: Hang Yu

item.title: Toward testing antinucleon$\unicode{x2013}$nucleus optical potentials with antineutron scattering lengths
item.description: arXiv:2608.18668v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The antineutron$\unicode{x2013}$nucleus scattering length is currently known only indirectly, via antiproton$\unicode{x2013}$nucleus optical potentials fitted to level shifts and widths of antiprotonic atoms. The antineutron$\unicode{x2013}$nucleus and antiproton$\unicode{x2013}$nucleus potentials are related to each other through charge symmetry. We calculate the scattering length from optical potentials proposed for antiprotonic atoms using nucleon density distributions as input. We find that the scattering length for an $N>Z$ nuclide is largely affected by the poorly constrained neutron density distribution and by a possible isovector interaction, one of the mechanisms introduced to reproduce the isotope dependence of antiprotonic $^{40,48}\mathrm{Ca}$ data. For $^{48}\mathrm{Ca}$, the isovector term modifies the scattering length by $0.3\unicode{x2013}0.4\,\mathrm{fm}$ ($0.4\unicode{x2013}0.5\,\mathrm{fm}$) for the real (imaginary) part, an order of magnitude beyond the uncertainty propagated from the isoscalar potential. As no antineutron$\unicode{x2013}$nucleus scattering data are available below $76\,\mathrm{MeV}/c$, a direct measurement with recently proposed low-energy antineutron beams would provide the first access to the antinucleon$\unicode{x2013}$nucleus interaction in the $s$-wave regime.
item.dc:creator: Hiroyuki Fujioka, Sayaka Ishii

item.title: Separable representations of two-body interactions for Faddeev calculations of light nuclei
item.description: arXiv:2609.08775v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Separable representations of the Ernst--Shakin--Thaler type are constructed for the charge-dependent Bonn (CD~Bonn) nucleon--nucleon potential ($j\le4$; $nn$, $np$, $pp$), for the Kanada--Kaneko--Nagata--Nomoto (KKNN) $\alpha N$ interaction, and for the Buck--Friedrich--Wheatley (BFW) $\alpha\alpha$ interaction. They are the input for momentum-space Faddeev calculations of $A=3$, $6$, $9$, and $12$ systems. The representations are tested against six acceptance criteria: off-shell accuracy at the pair energies sampled by the three-body kernel, phase shifts, effective-range parameters, bound and resonant states, and numerical stability.
item.dc:creator: M. M. Nishonov

item.title: The Fock representation of the Coulomb interaction. I. Two-body problem
item.description: arXiv:2609.16585v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the momentum-space few-body theory of light nuclei, where the Faddeev equations with separable two-body input close on one-variable amplitudes, the unscreened Coulomb interaction is exactly separable by the stereographic projection of Fock, with analytic form factors and strengths, and the truncation of the expansion converges at negative energies. It is derived here as an operator identity for the potential and added, without screening or fitting, as a block of separable terms to the separable nuclear input of a charged pair. The representation is compared with the screening--renormalization method and with Coulomb-distorted form factors on two-body benchmarks: the off-shell $t$~matrix, the Coulomb displacement of the $\alpha p$ Pauli-forbidden state, and the Coulomb-modified phases of the $pp$, $\alpha p$ and $\alpha\alpha$ pairs. The Feshbach--Schur projection of the Pauli-forbidden state is shown to require the Coulomb-dressed eigenstate, which the Fock block provides within the same separable problem. At positive energy a finite truncation is a screened Coulomb potential with an analytic, momentum-dependent radius.
item.dc:creator: M. M. Nishonov

item.title: The Fock representation of the Coulomb interaction. II. Three-body bound states
item.description: arXiv:2610.08520v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Fock representation of the unscreened Coulomb interaction, a block of separable terms with analytic form factors and strengths, is included in the momentum-space Faddeev kernel of three-body bound states beside the separable nuclear terms. A bound-state kernel evaluates every pair interaction at negative pair energies, where the representation is exact and convergent, so the Coulomb force enters without a screening radius and without a limiting procedure. With this representation the $^{3}$H--$^{3}$He splitting of the CD~Bonn potential is in very good agreement with the exact Faddeev result; in the $S$-wave model space the Coulomb-distorted form factors give about half the Fock value. The Feshbach--Schur projection of the Pauli-forbidden states acts on the forbidden eigenstates of the nuclear-plus-Coulomb pair Hamiltonian, the Coulomb-dressed states obtained inside the extended separable problem, as the eigenstate condition requires. The Coulomb displacements of the cluster-model states of $^{6}$Li, $^{9}$Be and $^{12}$C and of the $^{9}$Be--$^{9}$B mirror pair are given. The eigenstate condition is tested in $^{9}$Be and $^{12}$C by replacing the Coulomb-dressed forbidden states with those of the Coulomb-subtracted interaction and with the oscillator functions of the orthogonality-condition model.
item.dc:creator: M. M. Nishonov

item.title: Novel chiral-wobbling excitation mode in atomic nuclei
item.description: arXiv:2610.09808v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The properties of high-spin band structures in $^{74}$Br nucleus are investigated using the triaxial projected shell model (TPSM) and particle triaxial rotor (PTR) approaches. It has already been demonstrated that lowest three bands observed in $^{74}$Br have a characteristic feature of a chiral-wobbler. The first excited band is the chiral partner of the yrast band and the second excited band is the wobbling band based on the yrast state. We have analyzed the third excited band using the TPSM and PTR calculated quantities, and a unique character of this band is revealed. It is predicted that this band is the chiral partner of the second excited band, and is also a wobbling mode based on the first excited band.
item.dc:creator: Kouser Qureshie, S. P. Rouoof, J. A. Sheikh, Nazira Nazir, G. H. Bhat, S. Jehangir, N. A. Rather, R. J. Guo, S. Y. Wang, C. Liu, Q. B. Chen, S. Frauendorf

item.title: Why Stellar Sequences Turn Over: Fixed Points, Instability, and Equation-of-State Universality
item.description: arXiv:2603.26973v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We reformulate the stellar structure equations in the language of dynamical systems and show that the maximum mass of stellar sequences arises from the existence of a fixed point in the relativistic regime. In an appropriate representation of the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations, this fixed point becomes manifest and is directly associated with the turnover of the mass-radius curve. The existence of a fixed point implies an effective reduction in dimensionality near the onset of instability, which provides a simple explanation for several equation-of-state-insensitive relations and predicts new ones. In the weakly relativistic limit, we identify a complementary universal structure shared by stellar sequences at their maximum mass, which we term the "compressible limit," and derive distinct universal relations governing the maximum mass in the Newtonian and post-Newtonian regimes. Combining these theoretical results with current astrophysical constraints, we show that the J0740+6620 pulsar is unlikely to lie near the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff maximum mass unless the equation of state exhibits a strong first-order phase transition at densities just above its central density.
item.dc:creator: Isaac Legred, Nicolas Yunes

item.title: Hybrid neutron stars among mass gap objects are excluded by twin stars at $1.4\,M_\odot$
item.description: arXiv:2606.02593v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the question whether compact objects in the so-called mass gap ($2.5 < M/M_\odot < 5.0$) can be neutron stars or hybrid stars. Using a generic hybrid star equation of state with a first-order deconfinement transition, we map the allowed parameter space in a Seidov-type diagram and confront it with modern mass-radius constraints. We find that mass-gap hybrid stars require an extremely early onset of deconfinement and very stiff quark matter. The Bayesian analysis, however, favors equations of state with deconfinement at typical neutron-star masses around $1.4\,M_\odot$ with mass-twin stars that, if confirmed, would rule out hybrid stars as candidates for observed mass-gap compact objects.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Ayriyan, David Blaschke, Marcin Dubaj, Oleksandr Vitiuk, Adrian Wojcik

item.title: Full-event anomaly detection for new physics searches at the Electron-Ion Collider
item.description: arXiv:2610.00308v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The future Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) will offer new opportunities to search for physics beyond the Standard Model. We study resonant anomaly detection using machine learning and the full particle content of an event. We consider a new neutral gauge boson and a heavy neutral lepton as illustrative signals with different electron-jet topologies. Weakly supervised learning uses this event information to enhance the sensitivity of an invariant-mass search without identifying individual signal events during training. Comparisons with high-level observables show that the electron kinematics account for an important part of the separation, while correlations among the particles provide further sensitivity. We also construct a conditional full-event generator by adapting a model pretrained on LHC jets to produce EIC background events. A scan over signal fractions demonstrates substantial signal enhancement using the learned background reference, providing a proof of concept for this approach at the EIC. Finally, we consider a fully unsupervised graph autoencoder that provides modest signal enhancement but retains sensitivity at signal fractions too small for effective weak supervision. Our results motivate full-event anomaly detection as part of the EIC physics program and identify directions for developing methods suited to its distinct kinematics.
item.dc:creator: Dimitrios Athanasakos, Sebastian Grieninger, Hongkai Liu, Tymothy Mangan, Felix Ringer, Robert Szafron
